notes.kwanjula: La cérémonie de présentation; in francophone Africa, people often speak of la dot.
notes.ssenga: La tante paternelle: there’s no single French word for her role.
notes.embaga: Le mariage: both the wedding and the marriage.
notes.omugole: La mariée; the groom is le marié.
notes.amazaalibwa: L’anniversaire: also used for any anniversary.
notes.aliyekuja: Qui est venu; for a woman, qui est venue.

guidebook.intro: Celebrate introductions, weddings, birthdays and holidays. French has a set phrase for every occasion.

tips.title: Joyeux anniversaire, bonne année
body: Wishes use **joyeux** or **bon**: **Joyeux anniversaire !** (happy birthday), **Joyeux Noël !**, **Bonne année !**, **Bonnes fêtes !** To congratulate: **Félicitations !**
**Je te souhaite** + noun: **Je te souhaite un joyeux anniversaire.**

tips.title: La personne qui est venue
body: **Qui** links a description to a noun: **La personne qui est venue est mon frère. Les invités qui sont venus étaient contents.** It works for people and things, singular and plural.
Pronouns go before **avoir** in the past: **Je t’ai invité** (I invited you), **Je l’ai vu** (I saw him).

culture.title: La dot
body: In much of francophone Africa, marriage starts with a ceremony where the groom’s family brings gifts to the bride’s: **la dot**. Like the Ganda **kwanjula**, it is a big celebration with both families.
